issues.body: The round-4 issue remains. stub_with_timeout constructs sparq-oracle-stub-<pid>-<counter>.py under std::env::temp_dir(), writes it with fs::write, and executes that pathname. The symlink regression test similarly creates sparq-oracle-victim-<pid>.txt there with fs::write. Another local user can pre-create either predictable path as a symlink, so cargo test may overwrite an arbitrary file writable by the runner; the stub also remains replaceable between creation and interpreter access. Securing Scratch does not secure these separately created test artifacts.
issues.fix_hint: Place each executable stub and the victim inside private tempfile::TempDir instances, or use securely and atomically created NamedTempFile/create_new handles with owner-only permissions and retain their guards through execution. Execute only the securely created stub path. Keep only the inert planted symlink names directly in the shared temp directory.
issues.title: Test helpers still create predictable files in the shared temp directory

verdict.summary: Round 5 is stagnant: the production subprocess scratch files now use a private owner-only TempDir, but the round-4 major finding remains in the test code. stub_with_timeout still writes and executes a predictable PID/counter-derived Python file directly in the shared system temp directory, and the symlink regression test still creates its victim through a predictable PID-derived shared-temp path. A local user can pre-create either path as a symlink, causing the test runner to overwrite another writable file; the executable stub can also be replaced between creation and Python opening it.
